title: Making a run-and-gun boss rush with Claude Code: what worked for enemy patterns and boss fights
author: vinishkapoor
selftext:
Brasshail is a pixel-art side-scrolling shooter for the browser, with four short stages that each end in a boss. I wanted to see how well an AI coding agent handles the classic arcade stuff: tight controls, enemies that each need a different answer, and bosses with readable attack patterns.

**Who made what:**

* **Code:** all written with Claude Code
* **Pixel art, music and sounds:** CC0 assets from OpenGameArt and [itch.io](http://itch.io), all credited on the game page

**Workflow that worked:**

1. **Controls on an empty level first.** Run, jump, aim and fire, tuned until it felt snappy before any enemies existed.
2. **One trick per enemy.** Riot-shield troopers block frontal fire, snipers sit on high ground, and trucks and helicopters bring reinforcements. Describing each one’s single trick kept the code simple and the enemies easy to read in play.
3. **Weapons as drops.** Crates give a heavy machine gun, a shotgun or rockets, alongside grenades and a close-range knife. Balancing them so the starting pistol still mattered took a few rounds.
4. **Bosses one at a time.** A light tank, a giant walker, an attack gunship and a heavy siege tank. Asking for clear wind-ups before each attack made the patterns fair. Those fights took the most iterations.
5. **Fitting outside art to the code.** The sprites came from different packs, so hitboxes and animation timing had to be lined up with what the code expected.
6. **Polish last:** kill combos, coins for an Armory, screen shake, explosions and touch controls.

It runs in the browser on desktop and mobile, with no sign-up:  
[https://vinish.dev/brasshail-shooting-browser-based-game](https://vinish.dev/brasshail-shooting-browser-based-game)

If you’ve done boss patterns with AI, how did you get them readable without making them too easy?
